semantic_contract: A 21-instruction register-argument teardown method taking its receiver in ECX and returning nothing. It unconditionally delegates to 0x004ad280 with the same receiver; that callee makes two virtual calls on the receiver, at vtable slots +0x00 and +0x08, each handed the single stack argument 0x013ec468 (the address of a static float table holding 0.0, 1/3, 0.0, 0.0, 0.05, 0.2 and 0.35), then destroys every element of the pointer vector at receiver+0x18 by calling 0x00451400 on each element's first dword, and finally releases the vector storage with 0x00454280. Neither the vector nor any field is nulled by that pass. Back in the target, the single member at receiver+0x30 is tested for null and, only when non-null, finalised by 0x004b9570 with the member as the thiscall receiver and the owner passed as a second argument that the callee pops and never reads; that callee works on the sub-object at member+0x18. The function writes no field of the receiver and no global, so its entire effect is delegated. It is safe to call only with a non-null receiver: there is no null check on the receiver itself, unlike the check on field_30.
classification_rationale: The 21 instructions, the register-only ABI, the single field offset +0x30, the sole branch and its polarity, and the two-call structure are all read directly from the disassembly and corroborated by four disassembled callsites, so the mechanics are established rather than merely structural. It is nevertheless classified STRUCTURAL_ONLY and not BOUNDED_SEMANTIC because the function's entire observable effect is inside two callees whose semantics are only partially read: 0x004ad280 makes two virtual calls on the receiver's own vtable at slots +0x00 and +0x08 whose concrete targets were never resolved (no vtable for the receiver's class was located, and this address has no data reference from which to derive one), and 0x004b9570's two nested callees 0x004b98b0 and 0x004b97e0 were not read at all. A reader of this record can state what the function calls and in what order, but not what it accomplishes. It is not STILL_UNKNOWN because the body, ABI, field and control flow are fully known.
semantic_findings: The function is a thin two-step teardown: an unconditional base pass, then a guarded member finalisation.
The receiver is not null-checked; only the member at +0x30 is.
The member is read twice into two different spill slots, which is a compiler artefact rather than two distinct fields.
The owner pointer pushed for 0x004b9570 is popped by that callee's RET 0x4 and never read, so the member is finalised without any back-reference to its owner.
0x013ec468 is a static float table, not a type descriptor: 0.0, 1/3, 0.0, 0.0, 0.05, 0.2, 0.35.
0x004ad280 does not null the vector it empties or any field, so the pass is not idempotent and a second call is observable.

Two of the thirteen callsites, in Editors::cEditor::OnExit, call 0x004ad280 explicitly and then this function, which calls 0x004ad280 again on the same object -- a double base pass in the shipped build, recorded as observed rather than repaired.

Every callsite guards the call with its own null test and then performs an inline refcount decrement at object+4 followed by a virtual slot +0x00 call with argument 1 when the count reaches zero, so this function is the explicit teardown half of a Release sequence.
The address has 13 references, all direct calls and no data reference, so it is not a vtable entry and cannot be used to infer an owning class.
